Description: Talk to potential customers to understand their problems. NOT to pitch your solution. Use Mom Test: ask about their life not your idea.
When_To_Use: Before building anything|When pivoting|When confused about user needs
How_To_Do: Ask about past behavior not future predictions|Ask 'Tell me about the last time you...'|Never revealed your idea until end|Record and transcribe|5 interviews = pattern emerges
Output: Interview notes + pain point patterns + quotes
Anti_Pattern: Pitching your product in discovery calls|Leading questions|Asking 'Would you use this?'|Only talking to friends

Description: Teresa Torres framework: ask customers to tell stories about specific past experiences. Stories reveal real behavior not hypothetical answers.
When_To_Use: Continuous discovery during development|Understanding user workflows|Feature prioritization
How_To_Do: Start with 'Tell me about the last time you [did X]'|Follow up with 'What happened next?'|Map the story timeline|Identify pain points in the story|Link stories to opportunities
Anti_Pattern: Abstract questions ('Do you like X?')|Hypothetical scenarios|Not recording stories|Stopping after one story

Description: Quantify qualitative findings. Use AFTER discovery interviews to validate patterns at scale. Tools: Typeform, Google Forms, Tally.
When_To_Use: After 10+ interviews reveal patterns|For pricing validation|For feature prioritization|For NPS tracking
How_To_Do: Keep surveys under 5 minutes|Mix closed (rating) and open (text) questions|Sean Ellis PMF survey: 'How disappointed would you be if you could no longer use this product?'|Sample size: 100+ for statistical significance
Output: Data report with percentages + confidence levels
Anti_Pattern: Surveys before interviews (you don't know what to ask)|Too many questions (>15)|Only closed-ended questions|Low response rate (<10%)

Description: People don't buy products — they hire them for a job. Understand the job your product is hired for. Forces analysis: push (current pain) + pull (new solution) vs anxiety (change fear) + habit (status quo).
When_To_Use: When positioning product|When analyzing competitor switching|When designing features|When struggling with messaging
How_To_Do: Map the 4 forces: Push (pain of current) + Pull (attraction of new) vs Anxiety (fear of switching) + Habit (comfort of status quo)|Interview using switching timeline|Identify job statement: verb + object + context
Output: Job statement + forces diagram + switching triggers
Anti_Pattern: Confusing job with feature|Ignoring anxiety and habit forces|Too broad job definition|Not linking to actual switching behavior

Description: One-page business model. Test most critical hypothesis first (usually: do customers have this problem? Will they pay?). Each box = testable hypothesis.
When_To_Use: Before writing code|When pivoting|When explaining business to others
How_To_Do: Fill 9 boxes in order: Problem → Customer Segments → UVP → Solution → Channels → Revenue → Cost → Key Metrics → Unfair Advantage|Identify riskiest assumption|Design cheapest experiment to test it
Output: Lean Canvas + ranked hypothesis list + experiment plan
Anti_Pattern: Treating canvas as final plan (it's a hypothesis)|Not updating after experiments|Filling in Solution before validating Problem|No experiments — just assumptions

Description: Build landing page describing your product before it exists. Drive traffic. Measure conversion (email signup or waitlist). Validates demand without building.
When_To_Use: Idea validation before building|Testing messaging/positioning|Testing price sensitivity
How_To_Do: Headline = value proposition|Clear CTA (waitlist/email)|Drive 200-500 visitors (ads or communities)|Measure conversion rate|>5% email signup = strong signal
Output: Conversion rate + email list + traffic source data
Anti_Pattern: Over-designing the page|No traffic (building page but not driving visitors)|Counting signups as 'customers'|Not following up with signups

Description: Systematically analyze top 5-10 competitors: their positioning, pricing, features, reviews, weaknesses. Find your unfair advantage.
When_To_Use: Before entering a market|When positioning product|When losing deals to competitors
How_To_Do: List all competitors (direct + indirect)|Map features matrix|Read their 1-star reviews (= your opportunity)|Analyze pricing models|Identify their customers' unmet needs
Output: Competitor matrix + positioning gap + opportunity map
Anti_Pattern: Only looking at features (ignoring positioning)|Copying competitors|Ignoring indirect competitors|Analysis paralysis — researching forever

Description: The canonical PMF test: 'How would you feel if you could no longer use [product]?' If 40%+ say 'Very disappointed' → you have PMF.
When_To_Use: After first 50-100 active users|Quarterly PMF health check|Before scaling marketing spend
How_To_Do: Ask existing users (40+ responses minimum)|Single core question + follow-ups|Segment by user type|Track % 'Very disappointed' over time|Complement with retention data
Output: PMF score (% very disappointed) + qualitative segments
Anti_Pattern: Asking too early (before users have habit)|Small sample (<40 responses)|Ignoring the 'somewhat disappointed' segment|Only using survey without retention data

Description: Add a button/link for a feature that doesn't exist yet. Measure clicks. If high click rate → build it. If low → don't waste time.
When_To_Use: Feature prioritization|Demand validation before building|Understanding user intent
How_To_Do: Add feature in UI (button/menu item)|When clicked show 'Coming soon — join waitlist'|Measure click rate vs total users|Compare across feature ideas|Build the highest-demand feature first
Output: Click-through rate per feature idea + waitlist signups
Anti_Pattern: Not tracking clicks properly|Too many fake doors at once|Building anyway regardless of results|Not following up with interested users

Description: Build clickable prototype in Figma before writing code. Test with 5 users. Catch usability issues before they become expensive bugs.
When_To_Use: Before development sprint|For complex flows (onboarding, checkout)|When team disagrees on UX|For investor demos
How_To_Do: Create clickable Figma prototype|Recruit 5 representative users|Give them tasks to complete|Observe without helping|Note where they get confused|Iterate prototype
Output: Usability findings + revised prototype + confidence to build
Anti_Pattern: Perfect pixel design before testing|Testing with team members (they know the product)|Helping users during test|Not testing happy path AND edge cases
